checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the Merkle inclusion proof for blob_kzg_commitments in get_data_column_sidecars_from_block computed using the correct generalized index for the Fulu-fork BeaconBlockBody SSZ tree?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the implementation of get_data_column_sidecars_from_block in the client codebase. Locate the call to compute_merkle_proof(signed_block.message.body, get_generalized_index(BeaconBlockBody, 'blob_kzg_commitments')). 2. Enumerate all fields of the Fulu-fork BeaconBlockBody container in SSZ field order. Confirm that blob_kzg_commitments is at field index 11 (0-based) and the container has exactly 14 fields (inherited from Electra, with execution_requests appended). 3. Manually compute the expected generalized index: next_power_of_2(14) = 16, so gindex = 16 + 11 = 27. Verify floorlog2(27) = 4 matches KZG_COMMITMENTS_INCLUSION_PROOF_DEPTH. 4. Check whether the client hardcodes any generalized index value (e.g., from Deneb) rather than computing it dynamically from the Fulu BeaconBlockBody type. 5. Produce a test block with valid blobs and generate sidecars. Call verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof on every resulting sidecar and confirm the proof verifies successfully against the block's body_root. 6. Produce a sidecar with a deliberately incorrect proof (e.g., using a stale generalized index from a pre-Electra BeaconBlockBody) and verify that verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof returns false. 7. Submit the correctly-proofed sidecar to the gossip validation pipeline (data_column_sidecar_{subnet_id} topic) and confirm it passes the _[REJECT]_ rule for verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof.

code_locations.description: Calls compute_merkle_proof with get_generalized_index(BeaconBlockBody, 'blob_kzg_commitments'). This is where the proof is generated for the proposer's sidecars.
Verification side: calls is_valid_merkle_branch with the sidecar's inclusion proof, depth, subtree index, and body_root. Must match the proof generated on the proposer side.
Defined as floorlog2(get_generalized_index(BeaconBlockBody, 'blob_kzg_commitments')) = 4. Must be recomputed for Fulu's BeaconBlockBody if the SSZ layout changes.

Electra added execution_requests field (index 13), changing the total field count from 13 (Deneb) to 14. This could shift the SSZ merkle tree structure and generalized indices if the next_power_of_2 boundary is crossed.

executable_checks: Construct a Fulu-era BeaconBlockBody with valid blob_kzg_commitments and compute its SSZ hash_tree_root. Generate a Merkle proof targeting blob_kzg_commitments. Verify the proof against the body_root using is_valid_merkle_branch with the spec-defined depth and index.

Regression test: compute get_generalized_index(DenebBeaconBlockBody, 'blob_kzg_commitments') and get_generalized_index(FuluBeaconBlockBody, 'blob_kzg_commitments') and assert they produce the expected values (both should be 27 given current field counts, but this must be verified after any future field additions).

Negative test: generate a sidecar with a Merkle proof computed against the Deneb BeaconBlockBody layout and attempt verification against a Fulu block's body_root. If the layouts differ in generalized index, this must fail.
Integration test: propose a block on a Fulu testnet, produce data column sidecars, and verify that at least one honest peer accepts them without gossip-level rejection.

Client-specific audit: search the client codebase for any hardcoded generalized index constants (e.g., literal value 27 or any cached proof depth) and verify they are recomputed or updated for the Fulu fork.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0041 (validator-SG-004-INV-002). Trust Boundary: tb-014. The Fulu fork inherits BeaconBlockBody from Electra which added execution_requests as field index 13. While the generalized index for blob_kzg_commitments (field index 11) remains 27 in both Deneb (13 fields, next_pow2=16) and Electra/Fulu (14 fields, next_pow2=16), any future field addition that pushes the total past 16 would change next_power_of_2 to 32, shifting all generalized indices. Clients that hardcode the value rather than computing it dynamically are vulnerable to silent breakage across forks. The impact is severe: an incorrect proof causes ALL data column sidecars from the proposer to be rejected at the gossip validation layer, making the block's blob data completely unavailable and wasting the proposer's slot.

checklist.title: Verify that KZG_COMMITMENTS_INCLUSION_PROOF_DEPTH preset is consistent with the Fulu BeaconBlockBody SSZ tree depth for blob_kzg_commitments
checklist.test_procedure: 1. In the client implementation, locate the definition or computation of KZG_COMMITMENTS_INCLUSION_PROOF_DEPTH. 2. Verify it equals floorlog2(get_generalized_index(BeaconBlockBody, 'blob_kzg_commitments')) where BeaconBlockBody is the Fulu-fork version. 3. Compute the value manually: the Fulu BeaconBlockBody has 14 fields (inherited from Electra), next_power_of_2(14) = 16, blob_kzg_commitments is field index 11, so generalized_index = 16 + 11 = 27, and floorlog2(27) = 4. The proof depth should be 4. 4. If the client uses a fork-aware mechanism to select the proof depth, verify that the mechanism correctly selects the Fulu variant at FULU_FORK_EPOCH. 5. If the client hardcodes the proof depth as a constant, verify it matches the expected value of 4 for Fulu and that any fork-transition logic updates it appropriately.

code_locations.description: Consumes KZG_COMMITMENTS_INCLUSION_PROOF_DEPTH as the 'depth' argument to is_valid_merkle_branch

executable_checks: Unit test: assert floorlog2(get_generalized_index(FuluBeaconBlockBody, 'blob_kzg_commitments')) == KZG_COMMITMENTS_INCLUSION_PROOF_DEPTH

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is each data column sidecar deterministically published to the correct gossip subnet via compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(column_index)?

reachability.notes: This property guards the trust boundary (tb-010) between the validator node and the gossip network. The subnet computation formula subnet_id = column_index % DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT must be deterministic and consistent across all clients. A divergence would cause data column fragmentation, where sidecars are published to subnets that peers are not subscribed to, degrading data availability for the entire network.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. LOCATE SUBNET COMPUTATION IMPLEMENTATIONS: Identify the compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar function (or equivalent) in each consensus client. Reference spec: column_index % DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT (where DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT = 128). Known locations: (a) Lighthouse: consensus/types/src/data/data_column_subnet_id.rs, function from_column_index -- uses column_index.safe_rem(spec.data_column_sidecar_subnet_count). (b) Prysm: beacon-chain/core/peerdas/p2p_interface.go -- subnet computation uses params.BeaconConfig().DataColumnSidecarSubnetCount; gossip validation in beacon-chain/sync/validate_data_column.go. (c) Nimbus: beacon_chain/spec/network.nim, function compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar -- column_index mod DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT. CRITICAL: Nimbus has a static assertion 'doAssert DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT == NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS'. If these constants ever diverge in a future spec update, Nimbus code that uses column_index and subnet_id interchangeably will break silently. (d) Erigon: cl/das/p2p_utils.go, function ComputeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar -- columnIndex % clparams.GetBeaconConfig().DataColumnSidecarSubnetCount. (e) Lodestar: packages/beacon-node/src/chain/validation/dataColumnSidecar.ts, function computeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar -- columnSidecar.index % config.DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT. (f) Teku: subnet validation is performed in DataColumnSidecarTopicHandler.TopicSubnetIdAwareOperationProcessor, with MiscHelpersFulu providing the computation. (g) Grandine: helper_functions/src/misc.rs, function compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar. 2. VERIFY CONSTANT CONSISTENCY: For each client, confirm DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT = 128. Check that the constant is loaded from the correct config file (mainnet.yaml or the respective preset). Verify it matches the spec: presets/mainnet/fulu.yaml and configs/mainnet.yaml both specify 128. Check for hardcoded overrides or test-only values that could leak into production builds. The value was previously 64 during early PeerDAS development (see ethereum/pm Breakout-Room-Meetings/PeerDAS/Meeting 02.md reference), so verify no client retains a stale value of 64. 3. CROSS-CLIENT DIFFERENTIAL TEST -- SUBNET COMPUTATION: Generate a test vector of all 128 column_index values (0 through 127). For each column_index, compute subnet_id = column_index % 128. Since DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT == NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS == 128, each column maps to a unique subnet (subnet_id == column_index for all valid indices). Run this computation in all 7 clients and verify identical subnet_id outputs. Any divergence indicates a consensus-critical networking bug. 4. EDGE CASE: COLUMN_INDEX >= NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS: The spec defines column_index as a ColumnIndex (uint64). Verify each client rejects column_index >= 128 BEFORE computing the subnet. If a client performs modulo first without bounds-checking, a column_index of 128 would map to subnet 0, creating a conflict with legitimate column 0 data. Specific checks: (a) Erigon: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index >= clparams.GetBeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns before the subnet check. (b) Lighthouse: Verify DataColumnSubnetId::from_column_index is only called after column_index validation. (c) Lodestar: verifyDataColumnSidecar is called before computeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar in the gossip validation path -- verify this ordering is maintained. (d) All clients: Submit a crafted sidecar with column_index = 128, 255, 256, and 2^64-1. All MUST be rejected at the validation layer before subnet computation. 5. VERIFY GOSSIP VALIDATION ORDERING: The P2P spec mandates [REJECT] checks in a specific order. Verify that each client checks 'sidecar is for the correct subnet' (compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(sidecar.index) == subnet_id) early in the validation pipeline. If this check is missing or performed after expensive checks (like KZG proof verification), an attacker could waste validator resources by publishing sidecars to wrong subnets. 6. VERIFY PUBLISHER-SIDE CORRECTNESS: On the publishing side (validator producing blocks), verify that get_data_column_sidecars correctly iterates over all column_index values in range(NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS) and publishes each sidecar to the topic data_column_sidecar_{subnet_id} where subnet_id = compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(column_index). Check that the gossipsub topic name construction correctly interpolates the subnet_id (not the column_index, which happens to be the same when DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT == NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS but could diverge in future specs). 7. CONFIG DRIFT SCENARIO TEST: Simulate a scenario where DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT is changed from 128 to a different value (e.g., 64 for a future spec update) while NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS remains 128. This breaks the 1:1 mapping. Verify: (a) Nimbus: The static doAssert would fire at compile time, catching the issue. This is good but insufficient if the assertion is removed. (b) All other clients: Would they correctly handle the case where multiple columns map to the same subnet? Column 0 and column 64 would both map to subnet 0. Verify no client assumes a 1:1 column-to-subnet mapping in its data structures or gossipsub subscription logic. 8. INTEGER TYPE AND OVERFLOW CHECKS: (a) Verify column_index is stored as uint64 in all clients and the modulo operation uses unsigned arithmetic. In languages like Go and Rust, this is the default. In TypeScript/JavaScript (Lodestar), verify that the modulo operation handles large numbers correctly -- JavaScript's Number type loses precision above 2^53. Confirm Lodestar uses BigInt or a safe integer type for column_index. (b) Verify that DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT can never be zero in any client configuration. A modulo by zero would cause a panic/crash. Lighthouse explicitly handles this with safe_rem and an expect message; verify other clients have similar protection.

checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0042, Trust Boundary: tb-010, Invariant: validator-SG-006-INV-001/002, Assumption: asm-013. The formula is trivially simple (modulo 128), which means the primary risk is NOT in the arithmetic but in: (1) constant value mismatches between clients or configs, (2) Nimbus's assumption that NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS == DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT holding forever, (3) missing or out-of-order validation checks that allow wrong-subnet publishing to go undetected, (4) publisher-side code that constructs gossipsub topics incorrectly, and (5) stale constants from earlier PeerDAS development phases.

checklist.title: Verify Validator Node correctly constructs and publishes all 128 data column sidecars to their respective subnets after block production

reachability.notes: Supporting node check for actor-validator-node. An honest validator must publish ALL 128 column sidecars to the correct subnets. Missing columns or incorrect subnet targeting degrades data availability for the entire network.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. LOCATE SIDECAR CONSTRUCTION AND PUBLISHING CODE: Find the get_data_column_sidecars function (or equivalent) in each client. This function takes a signed block and blobs, computes cells and KZG proofs, then constructs 128 DataColumnSidecar objects. Reference spec (fulu/validator.md): for column_index in range(NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS), build sidecar with column data, KZG commitments, KZG proofs, signed block header, and KZG commitment inclusion proof. 2. VERIFY COMPLETE COLUMN COVERAGE: After get_data_column_sidecars returns, verify that exactly NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS (128) sidecars are produced, with column_index values covering the complete range [0, 127]. No duplicates, no gaps. A missing column means no peer subscribed to that column's subnet will receive the data. 3. VERIFY PUBLISHING LOOP: After sidecar construction, the validator must publish each sidecar to its corresponding subnet. Verify: (a) The publishing loop iterates over ALL 128 sidecars. (b) For each sidecar, subnet_id is computed as compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(column_index). (c) The gossipsub topic is correctly formatted as /eth2/{fork_digest}/data_column_sidecar_{subnet_id}/ssz_snappy. (d) The fork_digest used in the topic matches the current fork. A stale fork_digest from a previous fork would cause messages to be silently dropped. 4. VERIFY SIDECAR INTERNAL CONSISTENCY: For each constructed sidecar, verify: (a) sidecar.index == the column_index used during construction. (b) sidecar.signed_block_header matches the actual block being published. (c) sidecar.kzg_commitments matches the block body's blob_kzg_commitments. (d) sidecar.kzg_proofs are valid for the corresponding cells. (e) sidecar.column contains the correct cell data for that column_index (cells from all blobs at position column_index). 5. ERROR HANDLING DURING PUBLISHING: Verify what happens if publishing to one subnet fails (e.g., network error, no peers on that subnet). Does the validator: (a) Continue publishing to remaining subnets? (Good -- partial availability is better than none.) (b) Abort all remaining publishes? (Bad -- a single subnet failure would cause 127 other columns to be lost.) (c) Retry failed publishes? (Good if bounded.) 6. TIMING AND ORDERING: Verify that sidecar publishing occurs promptly after block production. Delayed publishing reduces the time window for peers to sample and verify data availability. Check if sidecars are published in parallel (good for latency) or sequentially (acceptable but slower). 7. DISTRIBUTED BLOB PUBLISHING PATH: For the code path where a validator does not have blobs locally and uses get_data_column_sidecars_from_column_sidecar (EIP-7594 distributed publishing), verify: (a) The same subnet computation is used. (b) All 128 columns are still published. (c) The reconstructed sidecars use the original inclusion proof from the received sidecar.

checklist.title: Verify Gossip Network rejects data column sidecars published to incorrect subnets and enforces deterministic subnet routing

reachability.notes: Supporting node check for actor-gossip-network. The gossip layer must enforce that sidecars appear only on their correct subnets. Without this enforcement, a malicious or buggy validator could pollute subnets with misrouted sidecars, wasting bandwidth and confusing sampling peers.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. LOCATE GOSSIP VALIDATION FOR DATA COLUMN SIDECARS: Find the gossip validation handler for the data_column_sidecar_{subnet_id} topic in each client. The spec mandates a [REJECT] check: 'The sidecar is for the correct subnet -- i.e. compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(sidecar.index) == subnet_id.' Verify this check exists and is enforced. Known locations: (a) Erigon: cl/phase1/network/services/data_column_sidecar_service.go -- checks subnet != nil && *subnet != computeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar(msg.Index). (b) Lodestar: packages/beacon-node/src/chain/validation/dataColumnSidecar.ts -- throws DataColumnSidecarGossipError with INVALID_SUBNET code and GossipAction.REJECT. (c) Prysm: beacon-chain/sync/validate_data_column.go -- checks compute_subnet == subnet_id. (d) Teku: Performed in TopicSubnetIdAwareOperationProcessor before reaching DataColumnSidecarGossipValidator. (e) Lighthouse, Nimbus, Grandine: Locate equivalent validation. 2. VERIFY REJECTION BEHAVIOR: For each client, confirm that a subnet mismatch results in a [REJECT] (not [IGNORE]). A [REJECT] causes the sender's gossipsub score to be penalized, deterring repeat offenses. An [IGNORE] would silently discard the message but not penalize the sender. 3. VERIFY SUBNET_ID IS AVAILABLE TO THE VALIDATOR: The gossip validation function must have access to the subnet_id from the gossipsub topic metadata. Verify that the topic handler correctly parses the subnet_id from the topic string /eth2/{fork_digest}/data_column_sidecar_{subnet_id}/ssz_snappy and passes it to the validation function. If subnet_id is not available (e.g., passed as nil/null/None), the check is skipped. CRITICAL NOTE: Erigon's code checks 'subnet != nil' before comparing, meaning the check is only enforced when subnet information is available. Determine if there is any code path where subnet is nil during gossip processing -- if so, this is a validation bypass. 4. VERIFY CHECK ORDERING IN VALIDATION PIPELINE: The subnet check should be performed EARLY in the validation pipeline, before expensive operations like KZG proof verification. This prevents resource exhaustion attacks where an adversary floods wrong subnets with sidecars that pass all other checks except the subnet check. Verify the ordering in each client: (a) [REJECT] verify_data_column_sidecar (structural validity, fast) (b) [REJECT] subnet check (compare two integers, fast) (c) Remaining checks (KZG proofs, inclusion proofs, etc., expensive). 5. TOPIC SUBSCRIPTION CORRECTNESS: Verify that each node subscribes to the correct set of subnets based on its custody groups. A node in custody group G should subscribe to all subnets corresponding to columns in compute_columns_for_custody_group(G). If the subscription logic uses a different mapping than compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar, the node will listen on wrong subnets and miss data it is supposed to custody. 6. GOSSIPSUB SCORE PENALTIES: Verify that [REJECT] for subnet mismatch correctly triggers gossipsub scoring penalties (P4 or application-specific penalties). Without proper scoring, an attacker can repeatedly publish wrong-subnet sidecars without consequence, degrading network quality.

executable_checks: Wrong-subnet injection test: For each client, publish a structurally valid DataColumnSidecar with column_index=10 to subnet 11. Verify the receiving node issues a REJECT and does not forward the message.
Score penalty test: After a wrong-subnet REJECT, verify the sender's gossipsub score is decremented. Monitor for subsequent peer disconnection if score drops below threshold.

Nil-subnet bypass test (Erigon-specific): Determine if there is any code path where the subnet parameter is nil when processing a data_column_sidecar gossip message. If so, the subnet check is bypassed and this constitutes a vulnerability.

Subscription correctness test: For a node with custody groups [G1, G2, G3, G4], compute expected subnets from compute_columns_for_custody_group for each group, then verify the node's actual gossipsub subscriptions match exactly.

Validation ordering test: Instrument each client to measure time spent in gossip validation for a sidecar published to the wrong subnet. Verify the rejection occurs quickly (before KZG verification) by confirming the processing time is under 1ms.
